title: Before and After
label: ch:ml-before-after
canDo: I can say that something happens before or after a named time or a named event.

payoff.summary: From cold: the two words that order events, and the ending they both lean on.
payoff.note: THE NOTE SURVIVED ALL FOUR STALENESS MODES -- the first one in this run that has. 'munpu and shesham are not taught' is exactly true, and 'pinne (then) is the nearest and it sequences TURNS rather than EVENTS' anticipates the domain check and is right: aadyaM (ML-C68-at-first, 2350) and pinne (ML-C64-then, 2090) are what the domain holds, both named by the note's own sentence, and no BEFORE/AFTER concept_tag existed to collide with. A note CAN be trustworthy, and this is what one looks like; the four previous tranches found one wrong about the CASE, two wrong about the DOMAIN and one simply FALSE. NO NEW GRAMMAR, AND THE EXAMPLES CHAIN OFF CHAPTER 102. Both words are postpositions leaning on the dative, so raNTu maNikku munpu reuses the exact form ML-C102-manikku built, and uuNinu shEshaM shows the dative's OTHER shape -- the -inu of ML-C06 -- on uuNu, owned since 930. That gives the chapter a true spine: ONE ENDING, FOUR JOBS. 'to' and 'for' from chapter 6, 'at' from 102, and now a seat for each of these two. The ordering lesson then separates the two PAIRS: aadyaM and pinne stand alone and order the TELLING; munpu and shEshaM cannot stand alone and order the EVENTS. Until this chapter the learner could order their own sentences and not the world. shEshaM LANDS ON KNOWN SCRIPT DEBT AND NOTHING CAN BE DONE ABOUT IT HERE. It needs U+0D36, which has no script lesson -- SCR-12's 'sha', which chapter 103 re-derived as 12 distinct tokens across 15 headword fields. It does NOT trip neverTaughtGlyphs, because U+0D36 appears inside other letter lessons' example words, which is the understatement lessons.d records. A script lesson placed HERE would not help: closure is measured in READING ORDER and shari needs that letter in chapter 1, so the fix belongs at the start of the book, not at sequence 3870. Recorded against HL-C407 rather than half-fixed, and the word is not avoided for it -- shEshaM is the word. ROMANIZATIONS COPIED FROM NAMED WITNESSES: the chillu at U+0D7B as n, from budhan, karshakan and adhyaapakan; U+0D36 as sh from shani, sharkkara and shaithyakaalaM; U+0D37 as sh-dot from ML-S121 and bhakshaNaM. munpuM and shEshavuM in the recall's romanization follow ML-C70-um's rule, the one HL-C400 narrowed: a word ending in the anusvara takes -vuM. THE THREE CEILINGS AND THE TOKEN SWEEP WERE RUN IN DRAFT, and the full suite passed on the FIRST run for the second chapter running. The sweep's only unowned residue is uuNinu, a joined form built from uuNu plus a taught ending, and two metalinguistic ending fragments.
